# Signed Surface Bundle Profile 1.0 (LLM Reference)

## Bottom Line Up Front

- The Signed Surface Bundle Profile defines the exact payload and bytes a publisher signs before a production host renders a Surface app.
- A valid artifact contains only `signedPayload` and a detached `COSE_Sign1`; protected `method_uri` and `kid` select the verification method and independently configured key.
- The preimage is the profile domain, one zero byte, and RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme bytes of the closed signed payload. The bundle digest is SHA-256 over those same bytes.
- Verification and admission are separate decisions. An authentic bundle still needs publisher/app trust, release policy, owning-schema, app-graph, actor, entry, and dereference checks.
- Pinned release mode admits allowlisted digests. Monotonic mode atomically rechecks and commits only after every host admission check passes.
- The historical v10 spike signatures are not production conformance vectors because they use a different domain, sidecar keys, and unsigned signer claims.

## Behavioral Essentials

- The Signed Surface Bundle Profile signs one closed payload containing publisher claim, release identity and sequence, complete App Manifest, and complete URL-keyed documents map; authentic bytes are not automatically admitted.
- The signed preimage is the exact profile domain, one zero byte, and RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the signed payload; the lower-case SHA-256 digest covers those same bytes.
- Only protected COSE headers select method_uri and kid. Sidecar methods, keys, signer names, signing times, affirmations, and raw-public-key bypasses do not affect verification.
- Acquisition, parsing, digest, signature verification, host validation, dereference, and rendering consume one immutable byte snapshot; refetch or mutation creates a new candidate.
- Pinned release mode matches an allowlisted digest. Monotonic mode atomically re-evaluates and commits only after host admission, so failed checks and concurrent conflicts never advance durable state.

## Semantic Capsule

The profile separates byte integrity from host admission. The verifier consumes
one immutable acquisition snapshot, constructs the domain-separated canonical
preimage, resolves the protected `kid` through independent deployment
configuration, and preserves the integrity receipt unchanged through later
checks.

Deployment trust decides whether that key may publish the signed app with the
selected method at `checkedAt`. Release policy then rejects unpinned, stale, or
conflicting payloads. In monotonic mode, the durable store atomically
re-evaluates and commits only after schema, app-graph, actor, entry, and
dereference checks pass.

`verified`, `failed`, and `unverified` report integrity, trust, and release
precheck outcomes. `admitted`, `refused`, and `unavailable` report the later host
decision. Sidecar keys, signer names, signing times, affirmation text, and raw
public keys never become verified facts.

## Conformance Essentials

- A conforming artifact validates against surface-bundle-signing-v1.schema.json and uses profile='formspec-surface-bundle-signing-v1', detached COSE_Sign1, protected method_uri, and protected kid.
- Verification distinguishes verified, failed, and unverified; host admission then distinguishes admitted, refused, and unavailable without rewriting the integrity receipt.
- Deployment trust must authorize the signed publisher and exact app or canonical app namespace, allowed method, key validity interval, and revocation state at host-observed checkedAt.
- A production implementation must refuse payload mutation, another signing domain, unknown or missing kid, raw-key or sidecar-key bypass, unsigned signer claims, wrong publisher or app, stale/conflicting release state, and failed host admission.
- The historical v10 spike signatures are not production conformance vectors because they use the spike domain, sidecar public keys, and unsigned signer claims.
